claims.text: High-entropy alloys intrinsically contain local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions create spatially heterogeneous internal stress fields.
The heterogeneous internal stress fields act as effective pinning sites for moving dislocations.
Local lattice distortions delay dislocation cross-slip during dynamic deformation.
Local lattice distortions delay dynamic recovery during dynamic deformation.
Delayed cross-slip and dynamic recovery enhance work hardening under dynamic loading.
Delayed cross-slip and dynamic recovery enhance ductility under dynamic loading.
Vacuum arc melting followed by homogenization can produce a fully solid-solution equimolar HEA retaining characteristic local lattice distortions.
Ordering or use of a simpler alloy system can provide a comparator with less pronounced lattice distortion.
Impeded cross-slip and recovery still permit distributed plastic deformation.
The proposed mechanism produces a balance of strength and ductility at high strain rates.
Relative to the baseline alloy, the HEA will exhibit increased strain-rate sensitivity.
Relative to the baseline alloy, the HEA will exhibit higher yield strength.
Relative to the baseline alloy, the HEA will exhibit greater uniform plastic deformation.
The proposed mechanism should operate from approximately 10^-2 to 10^2 s^-1.
The proposed mechanism should operate from room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures when phase transformations and recrystallization do not occur.
Excluding phase transformations and recrystallization prevents thermal softening or dynamic recrystallization from dominating the observed response.
The quantitative influence of lattice distortion on dynamic properties may vary with alloy chemistry, processing, and test parameters.
